clue.text: Two animals bound for cover

parts.note: a buck is a male deer
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A pair of creatures heading off to find shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound for cover' looks like animals running for shelter, but it means cloth bound on as a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff cloth traditionally used in bookbinding for the covers of books.

clue.text: R. Mugabe gives offence

indicators.note: gives in the sense of buckling or yielding, so the letters bend into a new shape

explanation.surface: The Zimbabwean leader causes upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Mugabe was the long-serving leader of Zimbabwe; 'gives' rearranges his initial and surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, a feeling of resentment.

clue.text: Soldier in full gear that creeps around at night

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: kit is a full set of gear or equipment
RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for soldiers

explanation.surface: A fully equipped soldier stalking about after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The krait is a venomous Asian snake that hunts by night.

clue.text: Here in Canada it's a pound over the fixed rate

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of doctored or rigged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Canadian price quoted as a pound above the set rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' looks like part of a fixed rate but is the anagram signal; 'over' just places the pound before the rest in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is a western province of Canada.

clue.text: Game in which Diana and Jack have nothing on — look!

parts.note: Di is the short form of the name Diana
a jack is a sailor, as is AB (able seaman)
O looks like zero, nothing
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Diana and Jack playing a game with no clothes on, and someone calling out to look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have nothing on' suggests nakedness; it just tacks O onto the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling toy and game, a spool spun and tossed on a string between two sticks.

clue.text: Literary type with a leaning to the right

definitions.text: Literary type with a leaning to the right

parts.words: Literary type with a leaning to the right
parts.note: seems to be a conservative writer, but type is printing type that slopes rightward

explanation.definitionFit: Italics are a sloping typeface used in printing, leaning to the right.

clue.text: Worker's joints are wonderful

parts.note: a worker is a worker bee, so worker's gives bee's
knees are joints of the leg

explanation.surface: An employee's knees are marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is written BEE'S KNEES.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee's knees is an idiom for something excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Gamble a great deal on a patched-up tyre

parts.note: a lot means a great deal

indicators.note: patched-up suggests a mended tyre, its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Betting heavily on a repaired tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a game of chance, a gamble on a random draw.

clue.text: State of the fraternity — rows among the monks

indicators.note: among means the rows are placed inside the monks

parts.note: monks are brothers in a religious order
lines are rows

explanation.surface: Arguments among the monks reveal the condition of the brotherhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like quarrels but means lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Brotherliness is the quality of fraternal feeling, the condition a fraternity should share.

clue.text: Sailor goes to and fro to see pop group

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: going to and fro means the sailor travels forward and then back, so his letters appear again turned round

parts.note: AB again, the same sailor on his way back

explanation.surface: A seaman travels back and forth to catch a pop concert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish band behind Waterloo and Dancing Queen is a famous pop group.

clue.text: Possibly end a better woman — even a saint!

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps a better woman could end up as a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, borne by St Bernadette of Lourdes, who saw visions of the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: Note to change flag

parts.note: F is a note of the musical scale
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A memo instructs someone to swap the banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or lose strength, which is what wavering or stumbling describes.

clue.text: Not a very bright lot, but sturdy

parts.note: thick means dim or slow-witted
a set is a group or lot

explanation.surface: A dim-witted bunch, but physically strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset describes a heavily built, stocky, solid body.

clue.text: Warder organising a fete gets in something to drink

indicators.note: gets in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: beer is something to drink

indicators.note: organising means the letters of a fete are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A guard arranging a party lays in some drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beefeaters guard the Tower of London; 'organising' is the anagram signal and 'gets in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London.

clue.text: It's not true that oil, in fact, needs changing

indicators.note: needs changing means the letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that oil really must be replaced is false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs changing' rearranges OIL and INFACT; 'in fact' looks like a link but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fictional is invented, made up, and so untrue.

clue.text: Coming from Lake Nyasa to land further north

indicators.note: Coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Travelling from an African lake up to a country to its north.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Nyasa (Lake Malawi) does lie south of the country named, so the surface is true geography.
explanation.definitionFit: The East African country lies north of Lake Nyasa, so it is a land further north.

clue.text: Black market trader's location

definitions.meaning: ... is a black tarry substance, as in ...-black
a stallholder's ... is the spot where they trade

explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is both a dark tar and the patch a street trader occupies.

clue.text: Put into liquidation

parts.note: looks like winding up a company, but means placing something into a liquid

explanation.definitionFit: To submerge something is to plunge it fully under a liquid.

clue.text: Close to a hypotenuse?

parts.note: the hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle

explanation.surface: Asking whether a triangle's slanting edge counts as being near something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the hypotenuse is described loosely as a long side, not defined exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside or next to something is being close to it, the plain adverbial sense.

clue.text: The late shift

parts.note: seems to be a night work rota, but a shift is also a loose dress worn late at night

explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a loose shift-like garment worn to bed.

clue.text: Poor side away from home fails to survive

indicators.note: poor suggests the word side is in bad shape and its letters jumbled

parts.note: out means not at home

explanation.surface: A weak team playing away cannot hang on.
explanation.definitionFit: A species or custom that becomes extinct has failed to survive.

clue.text: He finishes off game with the queen

parts.note: the kill is the game animals taken in a hunt
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone completes a match alongside the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes off' looks like completing a game but means kills.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer is someone who finishes off victims.

clue.text: Drive from A to B with mini, erratically

indicators.note: erratically means the letters wander into a new, irregular order

explanation.surface: A journey from one place to another in a small car, driven unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like motoring, matching the Mini, but means ambition; 'erratically' shuffles ATOB and MINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is the determination and desire to succeed, the same as having aspiration.

clue.text: Key to passage leading to kitchen

parts.note: G is a musical key
an alley is a narrow passage

explanation.surface: A key that opens a corridor into the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the kitchen on a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Error made by student before recess

parts.note: L for learner, a student
an apse is a recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: A pupil's mistake just before break time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' looks like a school break but is an architectural niche.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor mistake.

clue.text: Composer in far off New Zealand heard record

indicators.note: off means the word far is jumbled
heard means a word that sounds like the record is wanted

parts.note: a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A musician in distant New Zealand listens to a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges FAR to FRA; 'heard' turns LIST into its sound-alike LISZT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian pianist wrote the Hungarian Rhapsodies and is a famous Romantic composer.

clue.text: Game reserves

definitions.meaning: a cue sport played on a table with pockets
a shared fund or stock held for use

explanation.definitionFit: Pool names a billiards-type game and a common stock of resources.

clue.text: State what customs require travellers to do

definitions.meaning: to state is to announce formally

definitions.text: what customs require travellers to do
definitions.meaning: travellers must list dutiable goods at customs

explanation.definitionFit: To state openly is to announce, and at customs one must list goods on arrival.

clue.text: It reminds me repeatedly not to change

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word me appears twice in a row
to change means the letters of not are reordered

explanation.surface: Something keeps telling me not to alter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives MEME; 'to change' makes NTO from NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake serves as a reminder of a person or event.
